# Issue 118

Hello\! Happy new year. The last week where it’s appropriate to say it. The response to my last email was heartwarming. Thank you all. [Here it is in case you missed it](https://medium.com/devons-newsletter/issue-117-12-23-19-6ad362a124b0). I wrote about my start in the business. I’m pretty proud of it. I never know if I should air more personal or more industry with these things. I’ll try to intertwine the two whenever I can. I like it that way. Let’s begin.  
A few goals for this year. Make money. Write a script. Create.  
The script. I looked back at my goals the last five years. This has always been one. I’ve always failed. I can’t this year. Bums me out. I usually just ditch my stories because they end up resembling something else in the market \- like, I wrote a crispr inspired treatment that was pretty much The New Mutants (X-Men) meets Hanna (the film not the show). Gene editing is still so wild to me. Designer babies. Well, I have a new idea. It’s cool. I’ve been stewing on it for a few months and it took a turn for the better a week ago. It’ll be very cost effective and future forward. A contained, tech fueled thriller. First one to send me a shopping agreement wins. Please don’t. (:  
Speaking of writing, about a month ago I promised a piece on interactive media / design systems for content. I’ve been cooking it up. It’s partially a business plan. I’m not sure if I’ll share it yet. I might have to explore it with my friends in the space. Kick the tires so to speak. I smell opportunity. Hint: dig deep in the subliminal “responsiveness” nature of interactivity.  
I was doing some research for the essay and came across the patent for natural user inputs for interactive stories \- [here](https://patents.google.com/patent/US8381108B2/en?inventor=rudy+poat&oq=rudy+poat). It’s held by Rudy Poat along with his old Microsoft team that made Kinect and HoloLens. Rudy and John Gaeta are absolute geniuses. They’re behind bullet-time in The Matrix. Pioneers. Here is a [Gamasutra interview with them](https://www.gamasutra.com/view/feature/1802/beyond_machinima_rudy_poat_and_.php?print=1) from 2006 where they riff on interactive media, neural networks, and real-time rendering. A tad early, but now, the convergence, coalescence, is here. Cutscene creations, which I almost named my newco. I think [Otoy](https://home.otoy.com/) is going to own a good chunk of the space by laying down the bricks with their distributed render engine (and more). [Here is a piece](https://medium.com/render-token/media-in-2020-and-beyond-a-look-at-the-next-decade-60ae6fe60701) from their team predicting the next decade in media. Their advisory board is beyond stacked (J.J., Ari E, Eric Schmidt et al).  
Oh, something I noticed. FilmRise is releasing old movies for free on YouTube. I re-watched Memento over the holiday \- so good. [Here’s the link](https://youtu.be/KpNLhJhp8uI). (Tenet has me hyped.) The first film I made was a blatant rip-off of Memento, but so much worse. It was shot on 16mm. A fun experience. It’ll stay on my hard drive, never to be distributed. It was called The Break of Dawne. The detective’s name was Dawne. The title Good Will Hunting might’ve been a source of inspiration (eye roll). Tarantino once said, “I steal from every single movie ever made. If my work has anything, it’s that I’m taking this from this and that from that and mixing them together.” So I made myself believe that it was okay \- I was a kid\! I give myself a flier for that one. Begrudgingly. Back to FilmRise. They’ve raised a couple of decent sized film acquisition funds, all in the low to mid eight digits. Impressive. It looks like they might’ve bought the NewMarket catalogue (or licensed certain rights to it), which traded hands from Exclusive to Ambi. It wasn’t announced. Good for them.  
Enjoy all the favorite lists and prediction blogs in the collab section below. 1917 was my favorite film of the year \- very happy it won two Globes last night. I think we’ll see more micro-payments in the sub \$1 range. I hope so at least. I’d implement. Cue 402 error codes. “If I had a nickel” will be realized and widespread. That said, predictions are trite. Speculative. I just hope we all have a grand 2020\. My heart goes out to all those in Aus who might be affected by the fires. Devastating. Donate if you can. My cousins lost their home in the Kincade Fire in Sonoma in 2017\. Rain after fires can cause mudslides as well. Those wreaked havoc on Santa Barbara in 2018\.  
That’s all for now. Thanks for reading. See you next week.
